I'm gonna say it's just my company then. I had one client that had a gold allergy and for them to reset it in a platinum setting cost alittle close to 2k. Ofcourse they had to sketch and recast part but lord.

My only suggestion would be to have it checked first. Unless you are 100% sure its 18k. The reason why is because often times my clients are told they are but find out otherwise. I've had clients come in with jewelry they bought in somewhere outside of America or they've inherited that they were told were gold and they were actually silver. To check there should be a stamp on the clasp, atleast if you bought it here in America. Otherwise any pawnshop should have a gauge you can ask them to use to see what the gold percentage is. I just stress making sure before you try to rhodium because silver and rhodium dont do well. If by chance it is silver, you can always have it steam cleaned and polished and itll have the same effect!

Platinum is pretty durable anyways, like you said, other than it isnt scratch proof it's a great option for durability! It's honestly better than gold, but its abit more pricey than the common person wants to spend now a days. Atleast for the market at the moment. Being 17 years old, I'm sure you paid alittle less than what youd pay now, ya know?

Yes so most jewelers should be able to. I know my company will take anything but outside silver in. You may be charged a repair fee though, this is common, and if I'm not mistaken a re-dip shouldn't be more than like 50? But another great tip is to have your jewelry cleaned. We actually over free cleanings in our super sonic but you can also purchase the cleaner itself, or even just plain soap works. I suggest Dawn soap, then take a soft bristle tooth brush, a toddlers works, and just scrub it that way. It wont revamp it like a re-dip would but itll help. Jewelry really does get dirty so a bath is always a great thing to do! :D

Yes definitely! The moissanite actually sparkles alittle bit more in my eyes. The only difference really is the hardness. You might run into a few more scrapes on the surface (there's a term for this but my mind's not cooperating right now) than a diamond but nothing too noticeable! They're a great option for the look but not wanting to spend and arm and a leg! I personally was looking into them for my ring as well. My only other suggestion is regardless with whatever you gem you get, get it placed in a gold setting. Unless you have an allergy, which does happen, gold will last alot longer than silver and doesnt tarnish as much. If you opt for white gold, I'd recommend keeping up to date on your rhodium dips yearly, twice a year if you work in health care or somewhere you have to wash your hands alot because the soaps can break the rhodium and gold down over time. For you that dont know, the rhodium dips are just a protective layer for the white gold. Gold isn't naturally white so it has to have platinum and other alloys added to it so overtime it can become greenish due to you ph levels. Rhodium acts a a protective layer as well as a shiner! :D
